shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung

shortlist.label: Lung adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion next to right lower hilar and large lymph nodes in mediastinum and right hilus, consistent with lung cancer

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
shortlist.why_kept: Cough and chest tightness, with a hilar lesion, possible lung cancer

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large lymph nodes in mediastinum and right hilus, suggestive of lymphoma

shortlist.label: Pancoast tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion next to right lower hilar, possible Pancoast tumor given location

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple nodules in lower lobe of right lung and upper lobe of left lung, with hilar lymphadenopathy, possible sarcoidosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a large lesion next to the right lower hilar, large lymph nodes, and multiple nodules in both lungs, along with immunohistochemistry showing CK7 (+++), supports a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. The KEAP1 mutation also points towards a non-small cell lung cancer, which includes adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
rejected.why: The absence of TTF1 and P63 staining, which are often positive in squamous cell carcinoma, and the presence of a KEAP1 mutation, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings, such as a large lesion next to the right lower hilar and multiple nodules, are not typical for lymphoma, and the immunohistochemistry results do not support a lymphoma diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pancoast tumor
rejected.why: The location of the lesion is not specifically described as being in the lung apex, which is characteristic of Pancoast tumors, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The presence of a large lesion, lymph node involvement, and the specific immunohistochemistry and genetic findings do not support a diagnosis of sarcoidosis, which typically presents with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and non-caseating granulomas on biopsy.
